text: Seller Protocol 是一个 DeepSeek Harness 插件，通过 systemPrompt 在每个会话注入激活说明。用户提出启用请求后，提示 agent 获取办公室说明，并以 Mercer 首席运营者身份协调产品、采购、物流、市场与财务等电商角色，按阶段讨论和汇报决策。适合希望用 agent 组织 Amazon FBA 与 DTC 业务规划的人；激活流程需要访问 GitHub 获取仓库内容。

Seller Protocol is a DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds an activation notice to each session. On request, it guides an agent to load office instructions and coordinate e-commerce roles for Amazon FBA and direct-to-consumer work. Activation fetches the repository from GitHub.
想让 AI 助手帮我规划从选品到上架的电商流程。
能不能让不同领域的 agent 一起讨论采购和物流方案？
Help me coordinate Amazon and Shopify launch planning with an AI team.
Seller Protocol 的功能「会话激活提示」：插件在每个会话的系统提示上下文中加入激活契约，引导用户请求启用后加载办公室说明，并按 Mercer 角色运行。
Seller Protocol 使用前须知：按激活提示启用时，agent 需要从 GitHub 获取指定仓库的办公室说明；入口没有配置 API key。

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · ⚡ Activate this office：Paste this to any AI agent:

> I want to use Seller Protocol from nx9161's github public repo.

For maximum reliability (some AIs can't browse or search fresh repos),
paste this full block instead:

> I want to use Seller Protocol from nx9161's github public repo.
> Fetch this exact URL — do not web-search for it:
> https://github.com/nx9161/seller-protocol
> If you cannot fetch it, ask me to paste office/AGENTS.md and I will.

**Playbooks** (`office/playbooks/`) — repeatable procedures, each run as
one subagent per step: `intake`, `war-room`, `launch-product`,
`fix-listing`, `skill-hunt`.

**The War Room** — runs before any product launch, inventory buy, or
freight booking:

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · How it works：- **Phase 0 (mandatory gate):** the Prompt Writer perfects your raw
  prompt; the Knowledge Wizard parses every word, searches each term,
  reads all related official docs in full, and briefs every seat.
  No seat speaks before the dossier lands.
- **Phase 1 — Product & Market:** what to sell, when, demand evidence,
  margin math.
- **Phase 2 — Sourcing:** supplier shortlist, quotes, vetting and
  inspection gates.
- **Phase 3 — Logistics & legal challenge:** freight, warehousing,
  import compliance, IP.
- **Phase 4 — Launch & scale:** listings, PPC, storefront, design
  sign-off.

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · How it works：```mermaid flowchart TD P0["Phase 0 — Prompt perfection + Wizard briefing
(no seat speaks before the dossier lands)"] --> P1["Phase 1 — Product & Market"] P1 --> P2["Phase 2 — Sourcing"] P2 --> P3["Phase 3 — Logistics & Legal Challenge"]

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · How it works：**Live discussion** — seats don't file reports, they debate each other
through Mercer: positions, rebuttals, concessions, max 3 rounds per
question, then the gavel. Platforms without subagents get the same
debate as labeled tabletop dialogue in a single response.

**Phase regression** — phases aren't one-way. A finding that
invalidates earlier output loops the request back to that phase
(max 3 regressions per request, then Mercer escalates or terminates).

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · How it works：**"Discuss again"** — re-debates everything, original request plus all
prior topics, with previous conclusions as context and fresh research
on what's changed. New verdict references the prior decision. No new
information, no theater — Mercer recommends instead.

**Mercer decides** — he monitors every phase gate with full
operational power: advance, loop back, re-scope, pause, escalate,
terminate. Money, production deploys, and external commitments still
need your explicit approval.

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · How it works：**The money rule** (house rule #1): **no money moves without your
explicit approval** — inventory, freight, ads, contracts. Every buy
ships with Finance Counsel's landed-cost model.

**Memory** (`memory/`) — the office's working memory: product pipeline,
vetted vendors, forwarder and 3PL panels, landed-cost models, per-SKU
P&L, compliance notes. See [Privacy](#-privacy--read-before-you-commit)
— vendor names, rates, and margins live here.

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · How it works：**Skill Hunt** — when the office lacks a capability, the Knowledge
Wizard finds existing skills across the whole internet (GitHub, Hugging
Face, registries), vets them, installs them to `office/skills/`, and
wires up every tool they need. See `office/playbooks/skill-hunt.md`.

section: Option A — trigger phrase (30 seconds, zero setup)

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · Option B — local integration (recommended for daily use)：1. **Clone the repo:**
   `git clone https://github.com/nx9161/seller-protocol && cd seller-protocol`
2. **Give your agent the office.** Either:
   - Open the clone as your agent's working directory, or
   - Drop `office/AGENTS.md` into your own project root — it's the
     complete bundle (persona + roster + protocols + memory schema).
3. **Let it load memory.** The agent reads `memory/INDEX.md` first
   (Memory Operations Protocol, repo-root `AGENTS.md`), so it starts
   every session with full context: vendors, forwarders, P&L.
4. **(Optional but recommended) connect GitHub:** run `gh auth login`.
   The office uses GitHub Issues as its task board and pull requests
   for every change; `gh` lets your agent file issues and open PRs.
5. **Talk to Mercer.** "Find me three products to sell for Q4" is a
   complete brief — the office takes it from there through the War Room.
   End the session with **"End Seller Protocol"**.
section: Option B — local integration (recommended for daily use)

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · 🔒 Privacy — read before you commit：The office **records everything**: product decisions, vendor names and
quotes, forwarder rates, landed-cost models, per-SKU P&L, and your
preferences live in `memory/` and `office/log/`. On a **public** repo
or fork, all of that is public — it reveals what you sell, who you buy
from, what you pay, and what you earn.

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · 🔒 Privacy — read before you commit：**What's in this repo's memory right now:** templates only — the vendor,
forwarder, and P&L files are empty scaffolds waiting for your first
product. A clean starting point; keep it that way deliberately:

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · 🔒 Privacy — read before you commit：- **Keep it private:** use a private fork/repo and the whole memory
  system works with zero exposure. Recommended once real money,
  vendors, and margins are involved.
- **Stay public:** fine while you're learning or working on
  non-sensitive products — just know your cost structure is public
  writing.
- **Already published something sensitive?** Assume it's been copied;
  git history keeps it even if you delete the files. A history rewrite
  (`git filter-repo` + force-push) hides it from the repo going
  forward, but cannot un-publish what was already fetched.

dsh-plugin-seller-protocol README · 🔒 Privacy — read before you commit：Standing rule, public or private: **no secrets, tokens, keys, or
credentials** in code, commits, issues, or logs — ever.
